title: Revenue per Employee by Department
description: For each department, compute the **total sales revenue generated**, the **number of employees**, and the **revenue per employee** (efficiency metric). Join three tables: departments, employees, and sales.
solution_sql: SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(DISTINCT e.emp_id) AS employee_count, SUM(s.amount) AS total_revenue, ROUND(SUM(s.amount) / COUNT(DISTINCT e.emp_id), 2) AS revenue_per_employee FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.department_id JOIN sales s ON e.emp_id = s.employee_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.name ORDER BY revenue_per_employee DESC

test_cases.description: 3 departments: Sales(3 emps, $23000 total, $7666.67/emp), Marketing(2 emps, $9000, $4500/emp), Engineering(1 emp, $1300, $1300/emp)

hints: JOIN three tables: departments → employees → sales, linking on dept_id and employee_id respectively.
Use COUNT(DISTINCT e.emp_id) to count unique employees per department — using COUNT(*) would count each sale as an employee.
explanation: The three-table join connects organizational structure with revenue data. Sales dept: Alice(8k)+Bob(10k)+Carol(5k)=23k total, 3 employees → 7666.67/employee. Marketing: Dave(4k)+Eve(5k)=9k, 2 employees → 4500/employee. Engineering: Frank(1.3k), 1 employee → 1300/employee. COUNT(DISTINCT emp_id) is essential — without DISTINCT, multiple sales per employee would inflate the count.
